signals.claim: Enterprise SSD and NAND supply tightened materially by early December 2025 as AI/general-server demand accelerated while suppliers remained cautious on capacity, producing sharp contract-price increases and buyer inventory-building.

evidence.summary: TrendForce reported strong AI and enterprise-SSD demand, suppliers prioritizing high-margin products and retiring old nodes, and November mainstream NAND wafer contract-price increases of roughly 20% to more than 60%.

TrendForce said Q4 enterprise SSD conditions shifted from recovery to scrambling for components; CSPs were building inventory and average enterprise SSD contract prices were expected to rise more than 25% QoQ.

A large DataHoarder discussion documented consumer awareness of rapidly rising storage prices before the frozen signal. It is used as narrative-saturation evidence, not factual confirmation of supplier earnings.

contraryEvidence.summary: High memory prices were already creating BOM pressure and specification downgrades in end devices, so a memory-price upcycle should not be assumed to create unlimited downstream demand.

causalChain: AI inference/server expansion plus HDD constraints -> urgent enterprise SSD/NAND demand
cautious NAND supply expansion and node migration -> restricted bit availability
contract prices rise and buyers build inventory
a listed beneficiary must either own inventory at a favorable basis or sell scarce memory with enough margin leverage to offset working-capital and customer-price resistance
the opportunity ends when supply catches up, customer inventories normalize, or the company cannot convert market prices into realized gross profit/cash flow
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A direct memory supplier or authorized distributor with secured upstream allocation, material cloud/server customer exposure, evidence that rising memory prices improve realized gross profit rather than merely inflate working capital, and a valuation that does not assume a permanently tight memory cycle.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Near-term memory producer/distributor profit pools can expand as contract pricing rises faster than supply, but distributor economics depend heavily on inventory basis and thin gross margins.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Likely cyclical multi-quarter rather than permanent; supply response and buyer inventory behavior can reverse it.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The shortage narrative was already visible in industry media and enthusiast forums, so company-specific inventory basis and valuation are essential.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether an A-share company can capture the enterprise/server price spike directly enough to move earnings after financing and working-capital costs.

candidates.name: 香农芯创
candidates.economicExposure: The company's distribution subsidiary was an authorized SK hynix distributor and had established coverage of major Chinese cloud/internet customers. Its main distributed products included data-storage chips used in cloud services, data centers and mobile communications.
candidates.monetization: 2025Q1-Q3 revenue reached about RMB26.40bn (+59.9%) while attributable net profit was about RMB359m (-1.4%). The company has a direct channel into memory supply, but distribution margins are thin and rising chip prices can either expand gross profit on low-cost inventory or increase procurement/working-capital pressure.
earningsBridge: NAND/DRAM supply tightness and higher contract prices
SK hynix allocation plus cloud/server customer demand
inventory-basis and distribution gross-margin change
distribution gross profit minus financing/working-capital cost
attributable net profit and operating cash flow

basisReconciliation.externalIndicator: Enterprise SSD/NAND industry contract prices and supplier shortage indicators.
basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: The company is a memory distributor with SK hynix supply and cloud/data-center customers, but its sold product mix is broader than enterprise SSD and its realized distribution margin depends on purchase timing.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Enterprise SSD contract-price increases cannot be mapped one-for-one into distributor ASP or profit; inventory age, product mix, customer contracts, financing cost and upstream allocation matter.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: 2025Q1-Q3 operating cash flow remained slightly negative and the business carries large payables/borrowings typical of high-turnover distribution. Inventory basis is therefore a first-order variable, not a footnote.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Authorized upstream relationship and head cloud customers provide channel relevance, but distribution is lower-margin and less differentiated than owning scarce memory manufacturing IP.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several quarters if enterprise-memory shortages persist, but it can reverse quickly when suppliers add bits or buyers stop inventory-building.
normalizationIndicators: enterprise SSD/NAND contract-price increases slow materially
CSP inventory-building ends
company inventory rises without gross-margin improvement
operating cash flow deteriorates as procurement prices rise
upstream allocation improves enough to remove scarcity
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: The thesis is an inventory/contract-price cycle transmitted through a distributor, not a durable architecture monopoly.

candidates.priceExpectation: Pending deterministic pre-signal price and valuation enrichment. Candidate status requires proving that the cutoff valuation compensates for thin margins and working-capital risk.
contraryEvidence: Q1-Q3 revenue growth was strong but attributable net profit had not grown.
Distribution gross margins are structurally thin.

Was the company's on-hand inventory acquired cheaply enough to monetize the current price step-up?

signals.claim: AI data-center expansion created a severe upstream shortage of EML and CW laser light sources by December 2025, with 800G+ optical-transceiver demand accelerating and major buyers seeking secondary suppliers and alternative silicon-photonics light sources.

evidence.summary: TrendForce projected 800G+ optical-transceiver shipments rising from about 24m units in 2025 to nearly 63m in 2026, reported EML lead times extending beyond 2027, and said module makers/CSPs were seeking secondary EML and CW/silicon-photonics sources.

contraryEvidence.summary: The same shortage is accelerating alternate architectures and secondary sourcing. A beneficiary must be in the qualifying replacement path, not merely in the generic optical-component sector.

causalChain: AI cluster scale and 800G/1.6T migration -> much higher demand for high-speed optical links
limited EML/CW laser capacity and long qualification cycles -> laser source bottleneck
CSP/module makers seek secondary suppliers and silicon-photonics CW alternatives
domestic laser-chip suppliers already validated/shipping can gain volume, mix and potentially share
earnings persist only if qualification, capacity and yields convert the industry shortage into actual shipments
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A domestic InP laser-chip supplier already validated or shipping CW/EML products into 400G/800G data-center modules, with ordered/expandable capacity, high product-level earnings sensitivity, and a point-in-time valuation that does not require perfect 1.6T/CPO dominance.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: A genuine upstream bottleneck can expand laser-chip value capture and accelerate secondary-supplier qualification.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Potentially structural multi-year because 800G/1.6T deployment and qualification/capacity expansion take multiple quarters.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: AI optics was already a crowded theme; the incremental information is the severity and duration of the laser-specific bottleneck plus evidence of which suppliers can actually ship.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether domestic suppliers can scale qualified CW/EML output fast enough to capture shortage economics before incumbent/global capacity or architecture shifts relieve the bottleneck.

candidates.name: 源杰科技

candidates.monetization: The company sits directly at the laser-chip bottleneck. Data-center demand, higher-power CW products and EML qualification can expand volume/mix; the key constraint is production capacity, yield and customer qualification speed.
earningsBridge: 800G/1.6T optical-link demand and EML/CW shortage

gross profit and operating leverage
net profit and operating cash flow

basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: The company had already batch-shipped CW 70mW products into 400G/800G applications and completed 100G PAM4 EML customer validation before the cutoff.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Industry EML shortages do not map one-for-one to this company's revenue because its near-term volume mix was still heavily CW and each module/customer requires qualification.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: The business is capacity/qualification driven rather than inventory-price driven; equipment delivery, yield and capex execution are the main balance-sheet/cycle risks.
candidates.competitiveQuality: In-house laser-chip design/manufacturing, existing 400G/800G shipments and validated higher-speed products create a more direct bottleneck position than generic optical-component adjacency.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several quarters to years if 800G/1.6T optical demand continues faster than qualified laser capacity can expand.

signals.claim: Chinese export controls had created a severe ex-China yttrium shortage by December 2025, with critical energy/aerospace users stockpiling and overseas yttrium prices rising dramatically.

evidence.summary: Reuters reported GE Vernova was working with the U.S. government to build yttrium stocks after Chinese export restrictions created shortages; ex-China prices had risen dramatically during 2025.

contraryEvidence.summary: The shortage was created by export restrictions themselves, so a Chinese producer/exporter may be unable to monetize the overseas scarcity without licenses.

causalChain: export controls -> ex-China yttrium availability collapses
energy/aerospace/semiconductor users increase inventories and seek substitutes
overseas price rises sharply
a Chinese listed beneficiary only exists if it can legally monetize the scarcity or has a separate domestic/offshore earnings channel
headline overseas prices are not enough if export volume is constrained
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A producer with material, disclosed yttrium economics and a legally executable channel to monetize the shortage without being blocked by the same export-control mechanism.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Potentially large outside China, but the policy creates a direct monetization barrier for domestic exporters.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The physical shortage is clear; the listed-company mapping is not.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether any A-share company has material yttrium earnings exposure that can actually realize ex-China scarcity pricing under the export-control regime.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE. The shortage is real but the obvious A-share mapping is causally two-sided: export controls create the scarcity while potentially preventing domestic producers from realizing the overseas price. No clean point-in-time company earnings bridge was established.

signals.claim: Copper approached record highs in mid-December 2025 as mine disruptions and constrained supply met structurally strong grid/data-center/energy-transition demand, while 2025-2026 market balances were expected to remain in deficit.

evidence.summary: Reuters reported copper near USD12,000/t after a roughly 35% year-to-date rise, with mine disruptions, grid/data-center demand and surveyed market deficits for both 2025 and 2026.

contraryEvidence.summary: The same evidence showed copper had already risen about 35% in 2025 and was near record highs, making expectation saturation and company-specific cost/volume exposure crucial.

causalChain: mine disruptions plus slow new supply -> tight copper concentrate/refined balance
grid, electrification and data-center demand -> sustained copper consumption
high copper price expands mining margins for producers with owned copper output
integrated smelters may face offsetting low treatment charges, so mining exposure and smelting exposure must be separated
equity upside requires the cutoff valuation to understate sustainable mined-copper earnings rather than simply extrapolate record spot prices
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An integrated copper company with meaningful owned mine production, strong operating cash flow, enough mining exposure to benefit from high copper prices despite smelting-margin pressure, and a valuation that does not require record spot copper to rise indefinitely.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Higher copper prices shift profit toward mine owners, while concentrate scarcity can squeeze pure smelting treatment charges.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Cyclical multi-quarter with a structural demand overlay.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The copper rally was highly visible, so only company-specific mining exposure plus non-heroic valuation can justify a Candidate.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: How much of an integrated producer's earnings sensitivity comes from owned mined copper versus low-margin processing/trading and hedging.

candidates.monetization: 2025Q1-Q3 attributable net profit was about RMB6.02bn (+20.9%) and operating cash flow about RMB6.29bn. A higher copper price can improve mining economics, but the group-level bridge must account for its very large smelting/trading revenue base and hedging.

candidates.competitiveQuality: Large owned resource base, integrated processing and scale provide resilience, but integration also dilutes pure upside to a copper-price spike.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several quarters if mine disruptions and structural grid/data-center demand keep the balance tight; shorter if disrupted supply returns or demand weakens.
